newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cements, mills fling Cairo bourse to historic high.
newsitem.headline: Cements, mills fling Cairo bourse to historic high.

text.p: Cement and milling shares, and heavy buying by foreign investors, sent Egyptian share prices rocketing on Sunday to their highest level in history.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index soared 6.6 points to 260.54, breaking the record of 255.05, set on October 19, 1994.Turnover was a high 35.82 million ($10.54 million).
"Cairo is on its way to becoming an excellent market," said broker Walid el-Kholi of El-Rashad Securities Brokerage.
"Foreign investors are buying heavily and prices are going to rise exceptionally within the next few weeks."
Cement firms took the day's top spots, followed closely by the popular milling firms.
Helwan Portland Cement was the day's biggest gainer, rising 13.26 percent to close at 63.99 pounds.
The state, which retains a majority stake in the firm, said last week it was looking for an anchor investor to buy 10 percent of the company.
Helwan Cement increased net profits in the financial year 1995/96 by 21 percent to 125.52 million pounds ($36.9 million) from 103.61 million in 1994/5.
Privatised Amriyah Cement was the day's most actively traded stock, rising 1.00 to 60.50 in turnover of more than seven million pounds. Suez Cement also gained 3.50 to 57.50 pounds.
East Delta Flour Mills was also busy, with shares rising 4.75 to 50.00 in trade worth 3.1 million pounds.
But recent listing Upper Egypt Flour Mills was the best performing in its sector, rising 11.48 percent to 70.00.
North Cairo Flour Mills also closed higher, at 144.50 pound from 139.99 after it announced on Sunday it was doubling dividends for each of its six million shares.
The firm, one of the state's earliest and most successful privatisations, said it would give out an 11.25 pounds for financial 1995/96 compared to 5.04 a year earlier.
Brokers had expected the exchange to fix a price for privatised shares in Cairo Pharmaceutical and Chemical Industries CPIC.CA but now say it will take place on Monday.

The state offered investors 708,000 shares of the firm's 3.54 million shares at a minimum of 40 pounds a share for three days from November 19. The price will be determined by the bourse's "price discovery" mechanism.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 392.42 from 378.98 points on Thursday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 183.07 from 179.38.
Advancers outnumbered decliners 34 to 10. Twenty-two stocks traded but ended unchanged.
